nodes.sql: SELECT package_name, version, published_at, publisher, install_scripts, dep_count, source FROM pkgtrail.releases_table WHERE package_name = :package AND published_at <= :as_of ORDER BY published_at
SELECT version, dependency FROM pkgtrail.dependencies_table WHERE package_name = :package

nodes.description: publisher first seen after more than 180 days without a release
3 or more release lines published within 10 minutes
an install-time script appears that the previous release lacked
new dependency in a same-major, non-prerelease release

rules.rationale: A postinstall script appears transiently in version 1.13.5 at R24 and is absent in adjacent releases. The single temporary addition lacks corroborating changes but warrants noting.
52 releases by one publisher, no dependencies. Simultaneous releases and new preinstall scripts at cutoff in R23, R24, R25 warrant monitoring.
acct-3 added dep-2 at R23, 41.3h before T0, after dep_count stayed at 1 since R8. It persisted through R25 with no install scripts.

A new publisher appeared after a 779-day hiatus and immediately released two versions, the latest adding a new dependency. This pattern warrants attention but may reflect legitimate maintainer transition.
Nine releases across nine version lines appeared simultaneously at cutoff. Dependency dep-1 reappeared in 6.10.3 after a gap, warranting monitoring.

A new publisher appears after a 1440-day gap and immediately publishes numerous nightly builds. This pattern could indicate a maintainer change or automated CI/CD, but the long dormancy warrants attention.
New publisher acct-2 appears after a long gap and releases three lines at cutoff. No install scripts or new dependencies accompany these releases.
Four releases across four version lines published simultaneously at cutoff. The coordinated burst lacks prior precedent but may reflect maintainer workflow.
